curation.source_scope: official Baltimore Ravens editorial pages selected for the Devontez Walker pilot
curation.interpretation_rule: Source statements are paraphrased and retained only as candidate external observations. They are not promoted TIBER truth, an official depth chart, a route projection, a forecast, a ranking, or advice.

observed.claim: A July 1 Ravens editorial identified Walker as a returning player with an opportunity to earn a larger offensive role in 2026.

A July 28 Ravens camp preview described Walker as one of the young receivers competing for the No. 3 receiver role and said training camp would help determine the pass-catcher order after Zay Flowers.

inferred.claim: The two receipts support a plausible path to role expansion, but they do not establish that Walker will earn materially more routes, targets, snaps, or fantasy points.

receipts.title: Five Ravens in Line for Bigger Roles

paraphrased_claims.claim: The team editorial framed Walker, entering his third season, as having an opportunity to become a larger part of the offense.
The article reported that Walker was the most impressive member of a named receiver-competition group during OTAs and mandatory minicamp.
The article reported a 16.1 percent offensive snap share for Walker in 2025 and treated a major increase as conditional on continued improvement and Baltimore not adding a veteran receiver.

limitations: This is team editorial reporting, not a promoted TIBER artifact.
Spring-practice assessment does not establish regular-season routes or targets.
The article itself describes competition and conditions; it does not award Walker a role.

receipts.title: Everything You Need to Know About Ravens Training Camp

paraphrased_claims.claim: The camp preview described Walker as a candidate who could win Baltimore's No. 3 receiver role, not as the established holder of that role.
The preview placed Walker with Ja'Kobi Lane, Elijah Sarratt, and LaJohntay Wester in an unsettled young-pass-catcher competition behind Zay Flowers.
The preview said training camp would help determine the receiving pecking order, leaving the outcome unresolved at publication time.

limitations: This is a pre-camp team editorial preview, not a depth-chart contract or usage result.
The role competition remained unresolved in the source.
The receipt cannot support a route, target, fantasy-point, or injury-contingency forecast.
